newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-FIORENTINA PIN HOPES ON BATISTUTA REVIVAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FIORENTINA PIN HOPES ON BATISTUTA REVIVAL.

text.p: Italy's Fiorentina will be hoping star Argentine striker Gabriel Batistuta rediscovers the route to goal for Thursday's European Cup Winners' Cup quarter-final clash with Benfica.
With both teams struggling in their domestic leagues, success in Europe offers the chance of salvaging some glory from a disappointing season.
Fiorentina, with the usually prolific Batistuta suddenly finding scoring difficult, are languishing 12th in serie A only five points clear of the relegation zone.
Benfica are third in Portugal but 14 points adrift of title-holders and leaders Porto.
"It is a challenge that is going to stimulate both sides. We are going to do everything possible to make the next round," said Benfica coach Manuel Jose.
Both teams have injury problems and their difficulties are compounded by the fact that several key players cannot be used because they have already played for other teams in Europe this season.
Brazilian midfielder Alexandre Amaral, formerly of Italy's Parma, and Dutch winger Glen Helder, formerly with English club Arsenal, will both be watching from the stands.
But Benfica were given a boost by news that Brazilian playmaker Valdo Filho had recovered from an injury to his right leg and should be fit to start.
Fiorentina will be without Russian winger Andrei Kanchelskis, formerly of Everton, and injured midfielder Massimo Orlando.

The Italians however will be happy enough if Batistuta, their inspirational captain, can refind his touch in the first leg clash which also sees their Portuguese international midfielder Rui Costa line up against his old team.
Batistuta has been criticised for some seemingly poor performances recently but coach Claudio Ranieri is confident he will prove his worth against Benfica, twice winners of the European Cup.
Benfica - Michel Preud'Homme, Mario Costa, Jorge Soares, Jorge Bermudez, El Hadrioui, Jose Calado, Jamir Gomes, Tahar Kalej, Edgar Pacheco, Joao Pinto, Nica Panduru (or Valdo Filho).

Fiorentina - Francesco Toldo, Daniele Carnesciali, Pasquale Padalino, Giulio Falcone, Michele Serena, Giovanni Piacentini, Stefan Schwarz, Emiliano Bigica, Rui Costa, Gabriel Batistuta, Francesco Baiano.
